punchline: The Tao Te Ching says the softest thing in the world, water, beats the hardest.
thirty_sec: The Tao Te Ching, traditionally attributed to Lao Tzu, has eighty-one short chapters. Water yields to every vessel yet wears down the hard, and the text uses it to say that strength lies in flexibility. A living plant is soft and a dead one stiff. Wu wei is often understood as reading the flow instead of pushing against it.
